post.caption: A lost brooch cost under twenty pounds. In 1864, William Burges designed brooches for wedding bridesmaids. The Victoria and Albert Museum holds his drawings for nine of them, but the brooches themselves vanished long ago. Decades earlier, a buyer bought a silver brooch at an English antiques market. Its stones included lapis and coral. Antiques Roadshow's treasure hunt showed the old drawings, and the owner compared the brooch with one of them, and it matched. It later sold at a Gildings auction. It had cost under 20 pounds in 1988.
